truth: The buried Bell of Mercy will ring its final toll at midnight unless someone intervenes.
Saint Orra's miracle diverted the deaths of Grayhaven's citizens into refugees and attendants sheltered below the abbey.
The official casualty ledger omitted hundreds of refugees who entered the lower abbey during the siege.
Renewing the seal binds a living memory into the bell and perpetuates the victims' captivity.
The complete sealing rite requires the keeper's cadence, the original clapper, and a willing living memory.
The revenant called Ilyra was Elaria Nymm, registrar of the refugees and first unwilling anchor of the bell.
The original clapper can be released intact by pinning the third counterweight before cutting the black chain.
A cold-iron maintenance wedge in the cistern can immobilize the bell without breaking it.
Sister Mara renewed the seal twelve years ago and knowingly preserved the official lie.
Captain Severin Vale intends to remove the bell and use controlled tolls against Grayhaven's enemies.
The Orra Echo is a composite of the official saint-story and memories stripped from the bound victims, not Saint Orra's surviving soul.
The old civic ward-signs identify doors sealed by Grayhaven's siege guard rather than the abbey clergy.
Lucan Vey accepted a competing contract to recover the original clapper.
The liturgy of Saint Orra contains a repeated substitution where the name of a civic rite replaced a person.
The current Vale expedition answers to the challenge phrase 'The city outlives the innocent.'
At the fourth segment of the Midnight Clock, Severin's surviving soldiers enter the drowned nave.
At the sixth segment, the bell tolls and forces the most severe currently eligible ending.
